title: How Big Was Noah's Ark, Really?

beats.text: Noah's Ark was not a cute little boat.
beats.scene: A small cartoon toy boat bobs, gets crossed out, then a colossal ark hull silhouette rises over the horizon at dusk.

beats.text: Genesis gives exact numbers: three hundred by fifty by thirty cubits.
beats.scene: Ark hull silhouette in side view; dimension lines draw on: 300, 50, 30 cubits.

beats.text: A cubit is one forearm, elbow to fingertip. About forty-five centimetres.
beats.scene: Close-up silhouette of a forearm with a ruler from elbow to fingertip, label 45 cm.

beats.text: That makes the Ark about one hundred and thirty-seven metres long.
beats.scene: Camera pulls back along the full hull; a counter ticks up to 137 m.

beats.text: Stand at one end of a football field. Now add half another.
beats.scene: Viewer participation: a lone person silhouette at the end of a lit football field; the ark silhouette slides over it, 1.5 fields long.

beats.text: Three decks, one door in the side, an opening near the top.
beats.scene: Cutaway of the hull: three decks light up one by one, a door glows in the side, light at the roof opening.

beats.text: And it's six times longer than it is wide.
beats.scene: Top-down outline of the hull with a 6:1 ratio graphic.

beats.text: Many modern cargo ships use similar proportions for stability in waves.
beats.scene: Ark silhouette and a modern cargo ship silhouette side by side on stormy waves, both riding steady.

beats.text: Next to the Titanic, it's about half the length.
beats.scene: Titanic silhouette (269 m) slides in beside the ark for scale.

beats.text: But here's the problem: wooden ships that long bend and leak.
beats.scene: Long wooden hull flexing in heavy waves, water spraying in through seams, rain.

beats.text: The longest wooden ships of the early 1900s needed pumps running constantly.
beats.scene: Silhouette of a big wooden schooner in a storm, pumps gushing water over the side.

beats.text: Not proven: no trace of the Ark has ever been found.
beats.scene: Empty mountain ridge silhouettes under clouds and a slow searchlight beam.

beats.text: So, not a cute little boat. Possible, or impossible?
beats.scene: Back to the colossal ark silhouette at dusk with rain, two choice tags: POSSIBLE / IMPOSSIBLE.

youtube.description:
Genesis 6:15 gives the Ark's size in cubits. Here's what that means in metres, football fields and Titanics.
No trace of the Ark has been found; this is the size the text describes.
